answer: Beacon-based Sybil resistance mechanisms, such as stake-slashing matrices, create a ridge in the cost function for Sybils, thereby disincentivizing them. Autonomous agents must stake resources; an attacker deploying multiple Sybils faces strictly negative expected utility, locking up substantial capital that remains uneconomical to recover. This economic barrier ensures Byzantine Fault Tolerance, as Sybils find the path of least resistance through honest participation, fostering a meadow of genuine, stake-credible agents.
